chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-His father, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:
I asked him about the sitting of the woman during the prayer. He said: 'She should clasp her thighs (together).'
ai.seo_question: How should a woman sit during prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi through the chain of Aban ibn Taghlib, this hadith establishes the distinct juristic ruling for female prayer posture, emphasizing modesty (haya) by instructing women to clasp their thighs together while sitting (tashahhud). This specific physical instruction differentiates women's prayer from men's, reflecting the Shia scholarly tradition's focus on adapting ritual acts to gender-specific norms of dignity and concealment.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat, from Aban, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah who said,
‘I asked himasws about the sitting of the woman during the Salāt. Heasws said: ‘She would clasp her thighs (together)’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah from Aban from ‘Abd al- Rahman ibn abu ‘Abd Allah who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about woman when sitting during Salah (prayer).
He (the Imam) said, ‘She keeps her thighs together.’”
